queued.critic_reason: New family on an untested universe (us-treasury-daily, 0 tests) with a coherent risk-premium mechanism (inflation-risk term premium compressing as yields revert). The rule is fully causal (rolling 252-day percentile, 50-day SMA exit), H.15 yields are point-in-time and public, and Treasury CFDs exist. At the claimed net Sharpe of 1.2 over 10 fresh years, t is about 3.8 against a bar of 3.0, and two instruments traded as one book double the data; costs on liquid bond CFDs are small. Whether the edge survives is for the statistics.
queued.data_source: US Treasury daily yield data (Federal Reserve H.15) and corresponding CFD price data
queued.mechanism: Investors demand a premium for holding nominal bonds during periods of high macroeconomic uncertainty or inflation volatility. When inflation expectations spike, the required term premium increases, causing nominal bond yields to rise and bond prices to fall. Patient capital willing to bear inflation risk buys these bonds at rich yields, capturing the premium as expectations stabilize and yields revert. This persists because inflation risk is systematic and cannot be diversified away by most investors, who face constraints on holding long-duration assets during high inflation.
queued.rule: At the daily close, compute the 10-year Treasury yield. If the current yield is in the top 10% of the rolling 252-day window, enter a long position in the 10-year Treasury CFD. Hold the position until the yield falls below its 50-day simple moving average, at which point exit to cash. If the yield is not in the top 10% at the close, remain in cash. This rule spans 2 instruments (the 10-year and 30-year Treasury CFDs) traded as one book.
queued.title: Treasury Inflation Expectations Risk Premium
queued.why: at its claimed strength it expects t 3.795 against 3.0 (passes 79% of the time); the claim must be verified at its source before it is built
queued.why_new: This is the first proposal in the risk premium class on the completely untested us-treasury-daily universe. While the general bond risk premium is well-documented in academic literature, it has not been tested as a daily CFD trading rule in a swap-free account, and the specific mechanism of inflation risk premium compression captured via yield-percentile mean reversion is new to this lab's registry.

today.critic_reason: A real, mechanical flow story (vol-targeting CTAs must de-risk as realized volatility rises), implemented only from public daily commodity closes and prior-window volatility percentiles, so it is testable without look-ahead. It is not the closed VIX-contango or equity vol-managed family: it is a different asset class and a short-side breadth version (six instruments traded as one book over 12 fresh years), which is exactly the form the power-dropped volatility family was left open to. The claimed net Sharpe of 0.8 is modest rather than implausible; whether 12 years and a handful of high-vol episodes can clear a bar of 3.0 is for the statistics, not for me.
today.data_source: public daily commodity futures closes and CTA risk-model proxies
today.mechanism: Volatility-targeting CTAs are forced to sell commodity futures as realized volatility rises, creating temporary forced supply before rebalancing.

ways: about 14 years of fresh data at the claimed strength, against the 12 it has
or the same mechanism on about 2 independent instruments over those 12 years, tested as one book

today.rule: Enter short one unit per commodity in a six-instrument commodity futures basket when the prior 252-day realized volatility percentile is above the 80th percentile and the prior 10-day annualized realized volatility exceeds 30 percent; exit when the 30-day realized volatility falls below the 50th percentile of the prior 252 days or after 20 trading days, whichever first.
today.title: CTA Commodity De-Risking Shock
today.why: even at its claimed strength it expects t 2.771 against a bar of 3.0: as it stands it cannot pass, so it is not built as it stands. It is kept with a plan: about 14 years of fresh data at the claimed strength, against the 12 it has; or the same mechanism on about 2 independent instruments over those 12 years, tested as one book
today.why_new: Uses cross-commodity CTA forced de-risking thresholds rather than the single-asset VIX contango family already tested.

today.critic_reason: The rule needs a signed opening-cross imbalance series for a twenty-name basket plus the index, and dealer rebalancing-hedging proxies, at intraday granularity. No such history is held here (the universe is daily ETF closes) and the dealer-hedging measure does not exist as obtainable data; the hypothesis itself names no source. Even if the imbalance feed were bought, a 21-leg round trip inside 30 minutes at retail spreads is the exact configuration the record says loses its whole gross edge, so a claimed 0.6 net Sharpe over 8 years (t about 1.7 against a bar of 3.0) could not be supported.
today.mechanism: Dealer index-rebalancing hedging flows create temporary opening cross imbalances between the index future and a twenty-instrument basket of constituents.
today.rule: Enter long the basket leg and short the index leg with a fixed 1:1 notional hedge when the signed opening imbalance exceeds 2 times its 20-day rolling median; exit at fair value or after 30 minutes.
today.title: Opening Cross Imbalance from Index Rebalancing Hedging
today.why: The rule needs a signed opening-cross imbalance series for a twenty-name basket plus the index, and dealer rebalancing-hedging proxies, at intraday granularity. No such history is held here (the universe is daily ETF closes) and the dealer-hedging measure does not exist as obtainable data; the hypothesis itself names no source. Even if the imbalance feed were bought, a 21-leg round trip inside 30 minutes at retail spreads is the exact configuration the record says loses its whole gross edge, so a claimed 0.6 net Sharpe over 8 years (t about 1.7 against a bar of 3.0) could not be supported.
today.why_new: Uses live opening order-book imbalance and actual rebalance hedging proxies rather than close-to-close proxies.

today.critic_reason: Shorting the collateral after a forced-deleveraging event is the family already closed by evidence, not by power: LIQ-1's own liquidation events gave bitcoin +0.05% (t 0.07) over the next day, and 'shorting BTC and ETH CFDs after forced deleveraging' was dropped precisely because there is no continuation to sell. Swapping the trigger from derivatives liquidations to a lending-pool collateral ratio is the same mechanism on the same coins with no genuinely new evidence, and the historical pool-level collateral-ratio series is not held either.
today.duplicate_of: forced deleveraging / liquidation-led falls (LIQ-1, CASC-1; shorting after forced deleveraging)
today.mechanism: Lending-protocol collateral shortfalls force liquidations and borrower deleveraging, creating a transient forced selling cascade.
today.rule: When a lending pool collateral ratio falls below 150 percent and the prior 24 hours saw a greater than 5 percent price drop in the collateral, enter short one unit of the collateral; exit when the pool collateral ratio recovers above 200 percent or after 10 trading days.
today.title: Cross-Protocol Forced Deleveraging in Crypto Lending
today.why: Shorting the collateral after a forced-deleveraging event is the family already closed by evidence, not by power: LIQ-1's own liquidation events gave bitcoin +0.05% (t 0.07) over the next day, and 'shorting BTC and ETH CFDs after forced deleveraging' was dropped precisely because there is no continuation to sell. Swapping the trigger from derivatives liquidations to a lending-pool collateral ratio is the same mechanism on the same coins with no genuinely new evidence, and the historical pool-level collateral-ratio series is not held either.
today.why_new: Extends forced-deleveraging logic from derivatives liquidation to lending-protocol insurance cascades across venues.
